result:
If I could change the world in one way, I would eliminate the illusion of separation—the belief that we are fundamentally divided from one another, from nature, and from our own deepest selves. I would replace it with the unshakable understanding that everything is interconnected, that every act of kindness, cruelty, creation, or destruction ripples outward in ways we can’t always see.

I would make empathy not just a fleeting emotion but the default state of being, where no one could ignore the suffering of another without feeling it in their own bones. I would dissolve borders not with walls or laws, but with the realization that no human is illegal, no land is truly owned, and no life is more valuable than another.

And I would ensure that every person, from birth, was taught that their existence matters—not because of what they achieve, but because they are part of the vast, breathing web of life. No more hierarchies of worth. No more scarcity of love. Just the quiet, relentless truth: *We are all we’ve got.*

What would *you* change?
